title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM generates network configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded), N = 200 paired intents were executed across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns. Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference = 0.02; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (predeclared primary test). An archived paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]; this interval is reported as an auxiliary, descriptive/exploratory estimate distinct from the preregistered confirmatory McNemar test. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All numeric values, provider‑call accounting, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can accelerate intent→configuration translation in network operations (NetOps) but commonly produce mechanically detectable faults (syntax errors, reachability/topology violations, or ACL/policy mistakes) that pose operational risk. Prior surveys and prototype studies document both the promise of LLMs for NetOps and recurring evaluation gaps, notably the absence of provenance‑traced verifier integration and limited multi‑vendor emulation evidence [1]–[3]. Closed‑loop patterns that pair generation with deterministic verification and limited repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) have been proposed and shown in constrained prototypes to reduce mechanically checkable errors in code and configuration‑like artifacts [2], [4]. Motivated by open questions about multi‑vendor generality and verification cost, we preregistered and executed a paired, provenance‑traced Mininet‑style emulation study to estimate the effect of a verifier‑grounded GVR loop on the per‑intent incidence of operationally detectable policy violations.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys synthesize rapid growth in LLM‑for‑NetOps and highlight evaluation gaps such as benchmark provenance and verifier integration [5], [6]. Prototype and cross‑domain studies show LLMs can draft configurations but often introduce syntax, reachability, or semantic errors; verifier‑grounded repair and GVR architectures are recurrent mitigation patterns with empirical demonstrations in constrained settings (code generation, program synthesis, and limited configuration tasks) [2], [3]. Those prior works motivate our preregistered, paired evaluation that places a deterministic validator inside an emulated multi‑vendor template workflow and measures paired outcomes under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered (C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1) before any model calls. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — the difference in probability that an intent yields zero operationally detectable policy violations under guarded (GVR) minus baseline (single‑shot LLM) conditions. Design and sampling: a paired binary design with N = 200 unique intents (baseline and guarded episodes per intent), stratified across 3 vendor‑template families and 4 topology patterns (12 strata). Generation semantics and model: all generations used the declared model identifier gpt‑5‑mini as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json. The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and initial calls: by preregistration and execution semantics, exactly one sampled initial generation was produced per intent and that single sampled candidate was deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded conditions (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). Therefore any between‑condition difference within a paired intent can only arise from deterministic validation outcomes and the permitted verifier‑triggered repair call in the guarded pipeline. Validator and repair: the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checked syntax, reachability/topology constraints, and encoded ACL/policy constraints; the guarded pipeline permitted up to one verifier‑triggered repair call per intent. Execution budget and accounting: preregistered task_count = 200, planned_episode_count = 400, maximum_model_calls = 400, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Analysis plan: preregistered primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary success indicators; we report the paired risk difference and, secondarily, present a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) as an auxiliary descriptive interval. We explicitly treat the bootstrap interval as exploratory and not part of the confirmatory inferential procedure. Note: with very small numbers of discordant pairs the resampling percentile CI can, and in our archived results does, exclude zero even when the preregistered exact McNemar test is non‑significant; this methodological difference is discussed in Results and Discussion. Reproducibility: all task manifests, raw responses, deterministic validator traces, and analysis scripts are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/*, analysis/*) cited below.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: the run completed as preregistered (completed_episode_count = 400; complete_pair_count = 200). Provider audit and deterministic reconciliation report hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 (200 shared initial generation calls + 4 repair calls) and repair stage count = 4. Paired outcomes (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 196 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline succeed), n00 = 0 (both fail). Baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired risk difference = 0.02. Preregistered primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) yields p = 0.125 (no rejection at α = 0.05). Auxiliary descriptive estimate: archived paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04]; per Methods this interval is reported as exploratory and not a preregistered confirmatory interval. Repairs and cost accounting: four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked (repair calls = 4). Total model calls = 204 → mean model calls per intent = 1.02; mean extra calls per intent due to guarded repairs = 0.02; mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. Missingness and deviations: no pairs were excluded and no failed episodes occurred; deterministic_reconciliation reports no post‑preregistration deviations. Representative artifacts: example paired traces and validator summaries for tasks such as task-000004, task-000005, and task-000006 (shared initial candidate and both condition responses identical except for post‑validation repair where applied) are archived under execution/responses/* and execution/scoring/*. The exact contingency table and analysis metadata are archived at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.discussion: Confirmatory vs. exploratory inference: the preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test is the study's confirmatory inference (p = 0.125) and should drive formal claims about hypothesis rejection. The reported bootstrap percentile CI is an auxiliary descriptive estimator of effect magnitude; resampling intervals can exclude zero in sparse‑discordant situations (here n10 + n01 = 4) even when the exact conditional test does not reject. Substantive interpretation: within this provenance‑traced Mininet emulation and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic validator plus a restricted repair budget corrected all observed mechanically detectable baseline violations at low model‑call overhead (4 repairs across 200 intents). This indicates that, when a suitable deterministic verifier exists and can provide localized repair feedback, small repair budgets may correct the mechanically checkable subset of LLM faults at modest model cost. Limitations on generality and verifier coverage: results are confined to Mininet‑style emulation, synthetic vendor‑template families, a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), and a deterministic validator covering mechanically checkable properties; higher‑level semantic misinterpretations outside the validator's oracle may remain undetected. Threats to validity: (1) internal — shared_initial_candidate semantics guarantee paired differences derive only from validation/repair; (2) construct — validator scope limits detectable error classes; (3) external — emulation and synthetic templates constrain generalization to production hardware and other prompting or model strategies; (4) conclusion validity — low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger effect previsions in the preregistration. Practical note: all arithmetic and accounting claims (counts, p‑value, bootstrap parameters, model‑call totals) are drawn from archived artifacts and deterministic reconciliation and are not newly inferred beyond those artifacts.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation (N = 200 intents, shared_initial_candidate) of a verifier‑grounded GVR pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in a provenance‑traced Mininet emulation, the preregistered confirmatory test (exact McNemar two‑sided) did not reject (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR corrected the four observed baseline policy violations at the cost of four repair calls (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), producing an artifact‑grounded paired improvement of 2 percentage points (paired risk difference = 0.02). An archived paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04] is reported only as an auxiliary descriptive interval. These results show that a deterministic verifier plus a small repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations within this emulated setting at low model‑call cost; they do not establish production readiness nor coverage for semantic errors outside the validator. Future work should expand verifier coverage, evaluate multiple models and real vendor hardware, and increase sample sizes to better power small absolute improvements.

disclosure_statement: Declared models/tools and provenance: declared model gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; synthetic Mininet‑style harness. Autonomy boundary and human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Preregistration and artifacts: the study was preregistered as C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 and the preregistration preceded execution (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Generation semantics and temperature: execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1); the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Accounting: preregistered task_count = 200 paired intents; actual hosted model calls used = 204 (200 initial + 4 repairs); repair calls invoked = 4. Reproducibility: execution traces, deterministic validator traces, raw model outputs, analysis code, and manifests that substantiate reported numerical values are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/* and analysis/* paths referenced in the manuscript). No human manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not directly generalize to production hardware or live operational environments.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); high‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from validator‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); the low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduces power to detect small absolute improvements relative to some preregistered power scenarios.
